title: Lowering Input Lag: Tips to Optimize Your Wireless Controller Setup
summary: Cut controller lag with these proven tips. Wireless setup tweaks, connection methods, and settings adjustments that make your inputs feel instant.
body_text: You press the trigger. Half a second later, your character finally shoots. You're already dead. Input lag kills momentum in competitive matches. Even a few milliseconds of delay can be the difference between landing that headshot and getting sent to the respawn screen. The good news? Most wireless controller lag isn't a hardware problem. It's a setup problem. Here's how to fix it with your Turtle Beach gear. Why Wireless Controllers Lag in the First Place Wireless controllers need to send data through the air, and that takes time. Input lag below 16ms is excellent, while anything above 33ms becomes noticeable and starts affecting gameplay . But not all wireless is created equal. Standard Bluetooth connections often introduce 10-30ms of lag, sometimes more . Dedicated 2.4GHz wireless protocols cut that down significantly, typically sitting between 2-8ms . The real culprits? Wireless interference from other devices, outdated firmware, poor USB placement, and system settings that prioritize battery life over performance. Controllers like the Victrix Pro BFG Reloaded Wireless Controller are designed to minimize these issues through advanced wireless protocols. Use a Wired Connection When It Matters Most Wireless is convenient. Wired is faster. Period. If you're grinding ranked matches or competing in tournaments, plug in. A direct USB connection eliminates wireless overhead, dropping input lag to 1-4ms. The Stealth Ultra Controller gives you the flexibility to switch between wireless freedom and wired precision. Pro players default to wired for a reason. When milliseconds matter, cables win. The Stealth Pivot Controller also offers this versatility, adapting to your gaming scenario. Switch to Dedicated Wireless Technology Not all wireless connections are equal. Bluetooth trades performance for convenience. Turtle Beach's premium controllers utilize advanced wireless protocols that deliver superior performance over standard Bluetooth. These dedicated systems create direct links between the controller and the system, cutting out the middleman. The result? Lower latency, more stable connections, and fewer input drops during clutch moments. Eliminate Wireless Interference Your gaming setup probably has a dozen devices competing for airspace. Wi-Fi routers, wireless headsets, smartphones, Bluetooth speakers, and even microwaves can interfere with controller signals. Keep wireless receivers away from other electronics. Place them on your desk instead of behind your PC case. Position dongles closer to where you sit. Less distance means a stronger signal. A stronger signal means lower lag. Also, check your router. If it's sitting right next to your console or PC, move it. Wi-Fi and controller signals can clash, especially on crowded wireless channels. Update Controller Firmware Regularly Manufacturers release firmware updates to improve performance, not just fix bugs. Latency optimizations, polling rate improvements, and connection stability tweaks all come through updates. Check for Turtle Beach firmware updates regularly. It takes five minutes and can shave milliseconds off your input lag without spending a dime. Modern Turtle Beach controllers receive regular updates to keep performance sharp. Adjust Polling Rate Settings on PC Polling rate controls how often your controller reports its position to your system. Standard controllers poll at 125Hz (every 8ms). Gaming controllers can push that to 500Hz (every 2ms) or even 1000Hz (every 1ms). On PC, you can adjust polling rates through controller software or third-party tools. Higher polling rates mean faster input registration, but use slightly more CPU resources. For most setups, 500Hz hits the sweet spot. Console players don't usually get this option, but PC gamers should take advantage when using compatible Turtle Beach controllers. Disable Power Saving Features Your operating system wants to save battery. You want to win matches. These goals conflict. Power-saving modes throttle wireless performance to extend battery life. USB ports can enter low-power states. Controllers reduce polling rates when idle. All of this adds lag. On PC, disable USB selective suspend in power settings. Set your power plan to High Performance during gaming sessions. On console, keep your controller plugged in during competitive play to prevent battery-saving throttling. Enable Game Mode on Your Display Controller lag is only part of the equation. Display lag matters just as much. If your TV or monitor takes 50ms to show what your controller inputs, all your wireless optimization means nothing. Game Mode disables post-processing effects that add lag. Motion smoothing, dynamic contrast, and noise reduction all slow down the signal path. Game Mode cuts it out. Most modern displays have this feature. Turn it on. You'll notice the difference immediately, especially when paired with responsive audio from headsets like the Stealth 700 Gen 3 or Atlas Air . Keep Your Controller Charged A low battery doesn't just mean shorter play sessions. It can also degrade wireless performance. As batteries drain, signal strength weakens. Weak signals mean dropped packets and inconsistent latency. Keep your Turtle Beach controllers charged. Modern models feature intelligent battery management that maintains optimal performance throughout extended sessions. Building the Complete Low-Latency Setup Controllers represent one component of a lag-free gaming environment. The Stealth 600 headset provides clear audio without additional interference, while specialized controllers like the Victrix Pro KO leverless fight stick eliminate mechanical delays. Understanding differences between leverless vs traditional fight sticks for competitive play can inform your setup choices, while the ultimate couch gaming setup guide rounds out your optimization strategy. Conclusion Wireless doesn't have to mean laggy. The right setup tweaks turn wireless controllers into responsive, reliable tools that keep up with your reflexes. Plug in for tournaments, optimize your wireless setup for everything else, and stop blaming lag for missed shots. Your Turtle Beach controller is fast enough. Make sure your setup is too. FAQ What causes input lag on wireless controllers? Input lag happens when signals take too long to travel from the controller to the system. Wireless interference, Bluetooth overhead, outdated firmware, distance, and power-saving features all add delay. Is wired always better than wireless for gaming? Wired connections offer the lowest input lag, usually 1-4ms. High-quality wireless setups get close, typically 2-8ms. For casual play, modern wireless is fine. For competitive gaming, wired still has the edge. How much input lag is acceptable for gaming? Anything under 16ms is excellent. Between 20-33ms, sensitive players might feel a delay. Above 33ms, lag becomes obvious and affects gameplay, especially in fast-paced shooters and fighting games. Does Bluetooth add more lag than other wireless methods? Yes. Standard Bluetooth typically adds 10-30ms or more. Dedicated wireless protocols used in gaming controllers cut that down to 2-8ms, making them much closer to wired performance. Can updating controller firmware reduce input lag? Absolutely. Firmware updates often include latency optimizations, improved polling rates, and better wireless stability. Check for Turtle Beach updates regularly through official channels.

title: H2@Work Employee Spotlight: Tracy Parsons
summary: Tracy Parsons is a Manufacturing Engineering Technician at Plug’s Innovation Center in Henrietta, New York.
body_text: Tracy Parsons is a Manufacturing Engineering Technician at Plug’s Innovation Center in Henrietta, New York. Her journey from the Fuel Stack Assembly team to New Product Introduction shows her commitment to growth, innovation, and teamwork. With her hands-on expertise and problem-solving mindset, Tracy helps transform new ideas into efficient processes on the production floor. From Fuel Stack Assembly to New Product Introduction Tracy joined Plug in January 2022 as a production technician when the Henrietta facility was still being set up. After gaining valuable experience in fuel stack assembly, she moved into the New Product Introduction team. Today, she works with engineers to build, test, and document new products that will later move into full-scale production. How she found Plug Tracy discovered Plug through an advertisement about the Innovation Center in Henrietta. At the time, she was looking for a workplace that offered growth, challenge, and purpose. After researching Plug’s mission and learning about its role in building a cleaner future, she knew it was the right place for her. A special family moment One of Tracy’s most memorable experiences was working with her mother and daughter at her previous job. It was the first time three generations worked for the same company, and the experience brought them closer together. For Tracy, it was a meaningful reminder of how teamwork and shared values can make any job more rewarding. Facing tough challenges Tracy recalls 2023 as a challenging year when a cyberattack disrupted operations. At that time, she was in the Fuel Stack Assembly team, and the situation required quick thinking and coordination. With the support of IT and engineering teams, they found ways to capture important data and keep production moving to meet customer needs. Why hydrogen inspires her Tracy takes pride in being part of Plug’s effort to provide clean energy solutions. Knowing that her work supports a more sustainable world motivates her every day. Her life philosophy Tracy believes in living one moment at a time. She says that every goal comes with ups and downs, and the only way to move forward is to take one step at a time with patience and perseverance. Life outside work Outside of work, Tracy enjoys being outdoors, whether it’s hiking, hunting, doing yard work, or spending time with loved ones at weekend cookouts. She loves spontaneous adventures and believes in living more, laughing often, and loving endlessly.

title: Top 7 Biometric Attendance Machines for Small Businesses in 2026
summary: Discover the top 7 biometric attendance machines for small businesses in 2026, featuring SalaryBox Gama & FaceScan Pro for seamless payroll integration.
body_text: In today's fast-paced business environment, managing employee attendance efficiently is crucial for small businesses aiming to boost productivity, ensure accurate payroll processing, and maintain high levels of security. Traditional methods like manual registers, punch cards, or even passcodes and patterns are prone to errors, proxy registration, and time theft, leading to financial losses and administrative burdens. This is where biometric attendance devices come into play, revolutionizing workforce management with advanced identity authentication technologies. Biometric systems use unique physiological traits, such as fingerprints, facial detection, iris recognition, vocal patterns, or hand metrics, to provide tamper-proof attendance tracking. These biometric attendance machines eliminate malpractices like buddy punching, offer precise data on arrival times and departure times, and integrate seamlessly with payroll software for overtime calculation, shift management, and monthly attendance reporting. For small businesses, investing in a reliable biometric attendance device means improved employee monitoring, time efficiency, and overall productivity improvement. Why Small Businesses Need Biometric Attendance Systems in 2026 Small offices and mid-sized organizations often operate with limited resources, making manual conventional attendance methods inefficient. Biometric readers provide data security through breach prevention and encrypted storage, ensuring compliance with labor laws. Key benefits include: Security and Malpractice Prevention : Unique biometrics prevent proxy entries. Contactless Operation : Especially with face recognition and facial detection, promoting hygiene in high-traffic areas. Speed and Convenience : Quick recognition time (often under 1 second) with anti-spoofing features like 3D recognition or infrared for masks and varying lighting conditions. Scalability : Suitable for growing teams, with user capacities from hundreds to thousands. Integration Capabilities : Many support HR attendance sync, payroll software integration, and cloud management via Wi-Fi, LAN, or Bluetooth. Cost-Effectiveness : Reduced upfront cost for small setups, with low maintenance expenses and ROI through time theft reduction. When choosing a biometric attendance machine, consider factors like the number of employees, environment (indoor/outdoor with dust or weather resistance), smart features, and connectivity options. For small businesses, hybrid solutions combining fingerprint and face recognition often strike the best balance between accuracy, reliability, and budget. Face vs Fingerprint : Facial systems offer contactless identification and handle issues like dirty or worn fingerprints, while fingerprints remain durable in dusty environments. In 2026, trends lean toward AI-powered face recognition solutions with cloud-based attendance for remote accessibility, multi-site management, and auto-updates. These systems support distributed workforces with features like geo-tagging and mobile clocking. Now, let's dive into our curated list of the top 7 biometric attendance machines ideal for small businesses in 2026. Each entry includes real pros and cons based on user feedback and performance data. 1. SalaryBox Gama The SalaryBox Gama stands out as a cutting-edge biometric attendance device tailored for small businesses seeking seamless integration and advanced features. This AI-driven machine uses facial recognition with liveness detection, supporting hybrid modes for ultimate flexibility. Pros : Lightning-fast verification under 1 second, even with masks, ensuring speed and convenience in busy small offices. Seamless payroll software integration and cloud connectivity for real-time entries, overtime calculation, and monthly reports, perfect for accurate payroll without manual intervention. High user capacity (1,000+ faces) with excellent scalability as your business grows. Built-in Wi-Fi and mobile app support for remote monitoring and employee activity tracking. Robust data security with encryption, preventing breaches and ensuring compliance. Cons : Designed for growing teams, so it provides more advanced features than basic needs, allowing room for future expansion without immediate upgrades. 2. SalaryBox FaceScan Pro Building on the Gama's success, the SalaryBox FaceScan Pro is a premium face recognition attendance machine with access control capabilities, making it ideal for small businesses prioritizing hygiene and security. Pros : Advanced AI for 99%+ accuracy in facial detection, with anti-spoofing and support for varying lighting conditions. Contactless operation promotes hygiene in high-traffic areas, combined with RFID for backup. Direct HR/payroll integration for effortless shift management and real-time alerts. Inbuilt Wi-Fi, USB, and LAN for flexible connectivity options and easy installation. Vibrant HD display and spacious interface for user-friendly attendance marking. Cons : Its professional-grade features make it a future-proof investment, encouraging businesses to leverage full capabilities over time. 3. ZKTeco MB360 ZKTeco is a global leader in biometric systems, and the MB360 offers multi-modal authentication (face, fingerprint, RFID) in a compact design suitable for small offices. Pros : Versatile with 1,500 faces and 3,000 fingerprints capacity, plus Wi-Fi for cloud syncing. Fast recognition and basic payroll integration via SDK. Affordable entry-level pricing with reliable performance. Anti-spoofing algorithms for enhanced security. Cons : Limited advanced cloud features compared to dedicated payroll-integrated systems. Basic mobile apps may require additional setup for full remote access. 4. eSSL K30 Pro A popular choice in India, the eSSL K30 Pro is a robust fingerprint recognition device with push data technology, great for small businesses needing simple yet effective tracking. Pros : Handles 1,000-2,000 users with quick scans and access control options. Push data for real-time syncing and Excel exports. Budget-friendly with battery backup for power fluctuations. Easy installation and low maintenance. Cons : Primarily fingerprint-based, so less ideal for contactless preferences. Interface can feel dated; limited native cloud depth without add-ons. 5. Mantra MFSTAB Series Mantra's MFSTAB devices focus on reliable fingerprint and multi-biometric options, often Aadhaar-enabled for compliance-heavy small businesses. Pros : High accuracy with scratch-resistant sensors and large storage. Supports ERP/HRMS integration for payroll. Portable and rugged for varied environments. Cost-effective with good local support. Cons : More geared toward government compliance; may require extra configuration for pure private small business use. Limited facial options in base models. 6. Realtime RS Series (e.g., RS9n or T60) Realtime offers industrial-grade biometric attendance machines like the RS series, known for durability in small manufacturing or office setups. Pros : Strong fingerprint and optional face modes with TCP/IP connectivity. Affordable and easy to deploy for basic attendance tracking. Good for dusty environments with reliable sensors. Integrates with third-party payroll. Cons : Offline-heavy cloud features may need extra modules. Slower recognition in high-volume scenarios compared to AI-focused devices. 7. Biomax N-BM70W Pro The Biomax series provides Wi-Fi-enabled face biometric machines, suitable for modern small offices embracing contactless tech. Pros : Versatile face and fingerprint with Wi-Fi for cloud management. Access control integration and temperature options (post-pandemic relevance). User-friendly with good capacity for small teams. Competitive pricing with push data. Cons : May struggle in extreme lighting without advanced infrared. Integration depth varies; best for basic payroll syncing. Final Thoughts Choosing the right biometric attendance device in 2026 depends on your small business's specific needs, whether prioritizing contactless facial identification, seamless payroll integration, or budget-friendly durability. Devices like the SalaryBox Gama and FaceScan Pro lead with innovative AI, cloud solutions, and direct HR sync, making them top picks for efficiency and growth. Investing in these systems not only prevents time theft but also enhances workforce management, data integrity, and overall security. For small businesses, the shift to biometrics is a smart business investment yielding quick ROI. FAQs 1. What is the best biometric attendance machine for small businesses with payroll integration? The SalaryBox Gama or FaceScan Pro excels here, offering seamless sync with payroll software for automatic overtime calculation and accurate monthly processing. Examples from users show reduced payroll errors by up to 90%, making it a preferred choice over basic devices. 2. Are facial recognition systems better than fingerprints for small offices? Yes, especially for hygiene and speed. Devices like SalaryBox FaceScan Pro provide contactless operation with high accuracy, handling masks and lighting variations better than traditional fingerprints. 3. How secure are biometric attendance devices? Highly secure with encryption, anti-spoofing, and unique biometrics. SalaryBox models, for instance, use hashed data storage and SSL/TLS, ensuring breach prevention and compliance. 4. Can these machines handle remote or hybrid workforces? Many support cloud and mobile apps. SalaryBox Gamma integrates geo-tagging and mobile clocking, ideal for distributed teams. 5. What if power or the internet fails? Most have battery backup and offline modes. SalaryBox devices store data locally and sync when connected, ensuring no loss. 6. Is installation complicated for small businesses? No, most offer easy setup with Wi-Fi/LAN. SalaryBox provides intuitive interfaces and support for quick deployment. 7. Which device is most cost-effective long-term? Integrated solutions like SalaryBox Gamma save on admin time and errors, offering the best ROI for small businesses through productivity gains and precise payroll.

title: New Application Create Flow, Revamped Datastore Create and Update Flow, Multiple Node Groups, and Temporal-based Autoscaling
summary: We've introduced new application and datastore create flows, the ability to create multiple node groups, and Temporal-based autoscaling.
body_text: Application Create Flow v2 Users can now deploy multiple applications in one repository at the same time. Porter will now detect users’ stack when building with Github repositories. Revamped Datastore Create and Update Flow ‍ Users can now update their Porter-managed datastores from the dashboard. Additional support added for Elasticache metrics, all PostgreSQL versions, and snapshot/clone validation. New Dedicated Settings Page ‍ This page includes updated notifications options, including a PagerDuty integration, Slack , and email notifications for application CI and runtime alerts. Preview Environments Update ‍ Users can now dynamically create URLs based on branch names or PR numbers. Disk Updates Users can configure disk sizes per node group and will receive alerts when applications are impacted by disk pressure. Creating Node Groups Users can now create multiple node groups - example use cases for additional node groups include GPUs, spot instance for interruptible workloads, running nodes in a public subnet to reduce NAT gateway costs, and isolating compute demands across development, staging, and productions workloads running in the same cluster. Cluster Selector Update ‍ Clusters are now alphabetically sorted by default, and scrollable. Users can also keyword search for clusters. Temporal-based Autoscaling ‍ Porter can now monitor your Temporal task queues and automatically adjust worker count. More info in the docs here .

body_text: Piedmont Realty Trust, Inc. Signs over 475,000 SF of Leases Fourth Quarter-to-Date Bringing Year to Date Leasing to Approximately 2.3 million Square Feet December 8, 2025 PDF Version Atlanta, GA, Dec. 08, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Piedmont Realty Trust, Inc. title: Aldeyra Therapeutics Announces PDUFA Extension of the New Drug Application of Reproxalap for the Treatment of Dry Eye Disease
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Aldeyra Therapeutics, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: PDF Version LEXINGTON, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Dec. 15, 2025-- Aldeyra Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: ALDX) (Aldeyra), a biotechnology company devoted to discovering and developing innovative therapies designed to treat immune-mediated diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has extended the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date for the reproxalap New Drug Application (NDA) for the treatment of dry eye disease. The extended PDUFA target action date is March 16, 2026. Following submission on June 16, 2025, the NDA was accepted for review as a “complete class 2 response” by the FDA on July 16, 2025, with a target PDUFA action date of December 16, 2025. On December 12, 2025, the FDA met with Aldeyra to request submission to the NDA of the Clinical Study Report (CSR) for the dry eye disease field trial of reproxalap, for which top-line results were announced on May 5, 2025. The field trial, which was supportive of the activity of reproxalap relative to vehicle, did not meet the primary endpoint of improvement in dry eye symptoms relative to the vehicle control. Prior to submitting the NDA in June, the field trial was discussed with the FDA. At the December 12 meeting, the FDA made no other requests and did not identify any other specific issues with the NDA review. The CSR, which had been previously submitted to the Investigational New Drug (IND) file for reproxalap, was submitted to the NDA the same day of the meeting and was considered a major amendment to the NDA by the FDA. Per the FDA’s earlier request during the NDA review, the safety data from the field trial was submitted to the NDA on August 21, 2025. The CSR has been reviewed by the FDA under the IND. In early December, the FDA shared with Aldeyra a draft of the prospective label, and Aldeyra has submitted a response. The FDA notified Aldeyra that if no major deficiencies are identified during the extended review, the FDA plans to communicate proposed labeling requests and, if necessary, any anticipated postmarketing requirements by February 16, 2026. Conference Call & Webcast Information Aldeyra will host a conference call at 8:00 a.m. ET tomorrow, Tuesday December 16, 2025, to discuss the PDUFA extension. The dial-in numbers are (833) 470-1428 for domestic callers and (646) 844-6383 for international callers. The access code is 438712. A live webcast of the conference call will be available on the Investor Relations page of the company's website at https://ir.aldeyra.com . After the live webcast, the event will remain archived on the Aldeyra Therapeutics website for 90 days. About Aldeyra Aldeyra Therapeutics is a biotechnology company devoted to discovering innovative therapies designed to treat immune-mediated diseases. Our approach is to develop pharmaceuticals that modulate protein systems, instead of directly inhibiting or activating single protein targets, with the goal of optimizing multiple pathways at once while minimizing toxicity. Our product candidates include RASP (reactive aldehyde species) modulators ADX-248, ADX-246, and chemically related molecules for the potential treatment of systemic and retinal immune-mediated diseases. Our late-stage product candidates are reproxalap, a RASP modulator for the potential treatment of dry eye disease and allergic conjunctivitis, and ADX-2191, a novel formulation of intravitreal methotrexate for the potential treatment of primary vitreoretinal lymphoma and retinitis pigmentosa. title: Snapchat Recap 2025: Your Year In A Snap
summary: To help Snapchatters revisit their favorite Memories from 2025, today, we’re dropping this year’s Snapchat Recap.
body_text: December is always a time to celebrate and reflect on the moments, the laughs, and the friends who made the year unforgettable. To help Snapchatters revisit their favorite Memories from 2025, today, we’re dropping this year’s Snapchat Recap . The Snapchat Recap is a short video, individualized for every Snapchatter, with highlights from their Snaps, Stories, and Chats, offering a one-of-a-kind look at how they connected, communicated, and expressed themselves throughout the year. Across the board, 2025 was defined by friendship, creativity, and connection. From quick chats to long calls and everything in between, friends showed up for each other in more ways than ever. Here’s a look at some of the standout trends that captured how Snapchatters stayed close in 2025: Talking Made a Comeback Despite what the internet says, the phone call isn’t dead! In fact, talking on Snapchat kept climbing, whether through voice notes, voice calls, or video chats. Globally, Snapchatters talked for nearly 1.7 billion minutes every day on average — that’s nearly 30% more than last year. 1 And in the U.S. alone, over 5 billion voice notes were sent in 2025 — that’s nearly 10% more than last year! 2 Turns out, hearing someone’s voice is still one of the most powerful ways to stay connected. The Mundane is Meaningful Long gone are the days when you needed a big reason to reach out. Today, 40% of Gen Z Snapchatters interpret Snaps of random moments as a signal that you want to become closer friends. 3 In 2025, casual is cool when it comes to staying connected. Visuals Spoke Louder Than Words Features that offer quick ways of adding context, emotion, and humor are the norm. For example, Chat Reactions grew by 44% this year. 4 The ❤️ took the crown as the most popular of them all , 5 a universal shorthand for love, hype, and affirmation. 3 million more people also used stickers to communicate with friends this year , 6 another quick and visually expressive format to communicate more with less. Pop Culture Infiltrated the Chat From viral hairstyles to trending stickers, trends shaped how people represented themselves and communicated online this year. The most requested Bitmoji-inspired hairstyles of 2025 included the slicked-back bun, broccoli hair, and curtain bangs — a snapshot of the year’s top looks. And the 6/7 Bitmoji Sticker broke records to become the most-used sticker since its launch. 7 Another Big Year for the Group Chat The group chat was the heart of the action — where inside jokes were born and friendships stayed strong. Across the board, the number of people who send messages to group chats grew by more than 5% in 2025, 8 and some of the chattiest Snapchatters sent more than 8,880 messages to their top Group Chat this year. 9 That’s a lot of catching up! Happy holidays, and happy Snapping!

Auto-Data Entry into TMS: Clean, validated data posts directly into your TMS with no double entry. 8. Audit Trails + Analytics: Every decision is logged; finance leaders get real-time dashboards with visibility on exception rates and root causes, which leads to informed decision making. B. In addition, Lighthouz handles all complex freight scenarios: multi-stop shipments, Multi-load PDFs, missing pages, rotated scans, handwritten accessorials, LTL re-bills, POD bundling Lighthouz isn’t generic automation — it is freight-native intelligence. Strategic Benefits Beyond Numbers A. With automation, carriers and vendors experience fewer payment delays and errors, which enhances long-term collaboration and can even create opportunities for early payment discounts or negotiated terms. With automation, carriers and factors experience fewer payment delays and errors , which enhances long-term collaboration and can even create opportunities to get better rates. C. Scalability Automated AP teams can process 4–5x more carrier bills per person than manual processing. title: QuickLogic Announces Expanded Scope of Strategic Radiation Hardened FPGA Contract
summary: About QuickLogic: (NASDAQ: QUIK) QuickLogic Corporation (NASDAQ: QUIK) is a fabless semiconductor company that develops innovative embedded FPGA (eFPGA) IP, discrete FPGAs, and FPGA SoCs for a variety of industrial, aerospace and defense, edge and…
body_text: Total Contract ceiling has been increased to approximately $88 million over the span of multiple years QuickLogic has completed development of, and taped out a test chip that will be fabricated by GlobalFoundries on its 12LP process SAN JOSE, Calif. , Dec. 18, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- QuickLogic Corporation (NASDAQ: QUIK), a leading developer of embedded FPGA (eFPGA) Hard IP and User Tools, ruggedized FPGAs, and Endpoint AI/ML solutions, announces the scope of its Prime U.S. government contract for the development of Strategic Radiation Hardened (SRH), high reliability Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) technology to support identified and future Department of Defense (DoD) strategic and space system requirements has been increased to include GlobalFoundries 12LP fabrication process. With this, the total ceiling value has been increased to $88 million over multiple years. Under the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering (OUSD(R&E)), this project is sponsored by DoD's Trusted and Assured Microelectronics (T&AM) Program, and Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane is the Government's technical lead. "QuickLogic is honored to continue to lead the development of this highly specialized and mission critical program," said Brian Faith president and CEO of QuickLogic. "We are proud to announce that we have completed the design and tape out for an FPGA test chip that will be fabricated by GlobalFoundries on its 12LP process." About QuickLogic QuickLogic Corporation is a fabless semiconductor company specializing in eFPGA Hard IP, discrete FPGAs, and endpoint AI solutions. QuickLogic's unique approach combines cutting-edge technology with open-source tools to deliver highly customizable, low-power solutions for aerospace and defense, industrial, consumer, and computing markets.
